edges.description: The knock-in variant raises LRRK2-dependent Rab phosphorylation in mouse tissues and in patient blood cells, so VPS35 controls LRRK2 activity by a route not yet resolved.
Without normal WASH recruitment, retromer-dependent endosome-to-trans-Golgi transport of cargo is perturbed while plasma-membrane recycling is not.
The WASH complex is needed for autophagosome formation through trafficking of ATG9A, so its lost recruitment impairs autophagy directly.
Missorted cathepsin D and degraded LAMP2A remove, respectively, lysosomal proteolytic and chaperone-mediated-autophagy capacity.

Alpha-synuclein is a substrate of chaperone-mediated autophagy and of cathepsin D, so their loss is expected to raise its level; this has been shown in VPS35-deficient mice but not in D620N knock-in mice or in the one autopsied patient, which is why the target node is provisional.
Loss of degradative capacity in post-mitotic dopaminergic neurons is held to drive their degeneration; the intermediates are not resolved in this disease.
Fragmented, dysfunctional mitochondria are proposed to kill dopaminergic neurons; the knock-in line that shows fragmentation also shows nigral degeneration and heightened MPTP susceptibility.

nodes.description: Whether VPS35-related disease is an alpha-synucleinopathy is unresolved and the models disagree. VPS35-deficient mice and one D620N knock-in line (at 14 months) accumulate and aggregate alpha-synuclein in nigral dopaminergic neurons, and the trafficking defects remove two of its degradation routes. Against this, a second aged knock-in line shows no alpha-synuclein pathology and the variant does not modify the phenotype of A53T-synuclein transgenic mice, and the one autopsied carrier had no Lewy bodies and negative alpha-synuclein staining. The node is kept, and conformed to the module's alpha-synuclein anchor, so that this disagreement is recorded where the basket's mechanism would otherwise be assumed; its confidence is PROVISIONAL.

nodes.description: Retromer-positive endosomes are enlarged and redistributed to a perinuclear position in D620N cells and patient fibroblasts, and retrieval of cargo from endosomes to the Golgi is impaired: the cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor route that delivers cathepsin D to lysosomes, and in dopaminergic neurons the chaperone-mediated-autophagy receptor LAMP2A, which is instead degraded. The finding is contested: a third group saw apparently normal CIMPR and LAMP1 localisation in D620N cells. Two laboratories, one confirming the defect in patient-derived fibroblasts, outweigh one negative report, but the disagreement is recorded and the node is PROVISIONAL rather than ESTABLISHED.

nodes.description: The D620N knock-in allele strikingly elevates LRRK2-dependent phosphorylation of Rab8A, Rab10 and Rab12 in mouse cells and tissues, and Rab10 phosphorylation is raised in neutrophils and monocytes of heterozygous patients compared with healthy donors and idiopathic patients. nodes.description: Two degradative routes are compromised: macroautophagy, through impaired WASH-dependent ATG9A trafficking and autophagosome formation, and chaperone-mediated autophagy, through loss of its lysosomal receptor LAMP2A. meta.association: A heterozygous missense variant, c.1858G>A p.Asp620Asn, in VPS35 at 16q11.2 causes autosomal dominant late-onset Parkinson disease. The gene encodes the 796-residue cargo-recognition subunit of the retromer complex. The variant was found independently by exome sequencing of a Swiss and an Austrian kindred in 2011 and is the only VPS35 allele established as pathogenic.

evidence.reference_title: VPS35 mutations in Parkinson disease.
evidence.snippet: Exome analysis suggests that an aspartic-acid-to-asparagine mutation within vacuolar protein sorting 35 (VPS35 c.1858G>A; p.Asp620Asn) is the genetic determinant of disease.

evidence.reference_title: VPS35 mutations in Parkinson disease.
evidence.snippet: VPS35 c.1858G>A was found in all affected members of the Swiss kindred and in three more families and one patient with sporadic PD, but it was not observed in 3,309 controls.

evidence.reference_title: A mutation in VPS35, encoding a subunit of the retromer complex, causes late-onset Parkinson disease.
evidence.snippet: We found a missense mutation, c.1858G>A (p.Asp620Asn), in the VPS35 gene in all seven affected family members who are alive.

evidence.reference_title: A multi-centre clinico-genetic analysis of the VPS35 gene in Parkinson disease indicates reduced penetrance for disease-associated variants.
evidence.snippet: Our study apart from identifying the p.Asp620Asn variant in familial cases also identified it in idiopathic Parkinson disease cases, and thus provides genetic evidence for a role of p.Asp620Asn in Parkinson disease in different populations worldwide.

nodes.description: A third knock-in line, characterised with chronic ageing. At 14 months it shows progressive motor deficits, altered striatal dopamine and metabolites, robust loss of nigral dopaminergic neurons and striatal terminals, neuroinflammation, accumulation and aggregation of alpha-synuclein in dopaminergic neurons, mitochondrial fragmentation through the VPS35-DLP1 route, and heightened susceptibility to MPTP.
nodes.id: VPS35 D620N knock-in mouse (Niu et al.)

nodes.description: A heterozygous missense change in the cargo-recognition subunit of the retromer complex. The mutant protein folds and assembles with VPS26 and VPS29 normally, so the lesion is not loss of the complex but a change in what it can bind: the adaptor interaction with the WASH complex subunit FAM21 is weakened, which is the molecular function bound here. Whether the net effect is a partial loss of retromer function, a gain of function through LRRK2 activation, or both is contested (see the CONTROVERSY discussion), so no functional-impact category is asserted.

evidence.reference_title: VPS35 mutations in Parkinson disease.
evidence.snippet: VPS35 is a central component of the retromer cargo-recognition complex, is critical for endosome-trans-golgi trafficking and membrane-protein recycling, and is evolutionarily highly conserved.

evidence.reference_title: The Vps35 D620N mutation linked to Parkinson's disease disrupts the cargo sorting function of retromer.
evidence.snippet: Vps35 D620N is correctly folded and binds Vps29 and Vps26A with the same affinity as wild-type Vps35.

nodes.description: CRISPR-generated knock-in expressing the mouse orthologue of the patient variant at endogenous levels. Neither heterozygous nor homozygous mice died prematurely or showed clear neurodegeneration to 70 weeks; homozygotes had reduced potassium-evoked striatal dopamine release, and D620N/null compound heterozygotes had a survival disadvantage.

nodes.description: c.1858G>A, the only VPS35 variant established as pathogenic. It segregates with disease in Swiss, Austrian and further kindreds and is absent from thousands of controls. The protein is correctly folded and binds its retromer partners VPS26 and VPS29 normally; its defect is in binding the WASH complex.
